question: What is the main difference between laws and ethics in nursing practice?

options.A: Laws set the minimum legal boundaries while ethics guide moral excellence
options.B: Ethics carry prison sentences while laws only result in job loss
options.C: Ethics are written by parliament while laws are created by hospitals
options.D: Laws apply only to doctors while ethics apply only to nurses

explanation: Laws establish mandatory rules with legal penalties, whereas ethics provide a moral framework for striving toward fair and compassionate care. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T8#GNS216_U1_T8_h1)

question: What makes hepatorenal syndrome different from regular kidney failure?

options.A: Kidneys stop working because of high blood sugar
options.B: It only happens to people with healthy livers
options.C: It causes permanent physical damage to kidney tissue
options.D: The kidneys fail due to altered blood flow, not physical injury

explanation: Spot on! Hepatorenal syndrome happens because of severe blood circulation changes caused by liver issues—the kidney tissue itself isn't physically damaged at first. Excellent clinical insight!

question: A hospital ward manager reads a newly published study proving a new dressing reduces infection rates. What action represents utilizing this research?

options.A: Scolding staff nurses for not discovering the dressing themselves
options.B: Filing the journal away in a drawer for future decoration
options.C: Ignoring the study because the old dressing is cheaper to buy
options.D: Updating the ward's wound care policy to adopt the new dressing

explanation: Utilizing research means putting proven evidence-based changes into active clinical practice. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h7)

question: Which sign is most characteristic of the compensated stage of shock?

options.A: Normal blood pressure maintained by compensatory mechanisms
options.B: Slow, bounding pulse with warm, flushed skin
options.C: Severe drop in blood pressure and clear fluid overload
options.D: Unresponsive patient with zero urine output

explanation: In the compensated stage, the body successfully uses heart rate and blood vessel tightening to keep blood pressure within normal limits. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which side effect is a patient most likely to report right after using a rescue inhaler?

options.A: Severe swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Extreme drowsiness and a very low heart rate
options.C: Sudden loss of vision in both eyes
options.D: Fine tremors in the hands and a racing heart

explanation: Don't panic if a patient's hands shake a bit or their heart beats fast after a rescue inhaler—that's a normal, expected side effect of the medicine spreading through the body!

question: Why must on-site spotters communicate with the command center so quickly?

options.A: To allow rapid intervention before minor crowding turns into a crisis
options.B: To ensure ticket sales data is updated every minute
options.C: To prevent performers from starting their show too early
options.D: To coordinate food delivery schedules for vendors

explanation: Spotting a bottleneck early and radioing the team straight away can stop a small crowd crush before it ever starts.

question: Which lab test must be checked regularly for a patient on testosterone replacement therapy?

options.A: Prostate-specific antigen
options.B: Fastin blood glucose
options.C: Serum creatinine levels
options.D: White blood cell count

explanation: We keep an eye on prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels because extra testosterone can encourage the prostate to grow.

question: When doing home visits, what makes spotting gender-based violence different from working in a hospital?

options.A: Screening protocols are strictly enforced by hospital boards
options.B: Patients have continuous access to security personnel
options.C: Family members are legally barred from entering the room
options.D: Nurses step into private spaces where abuse can be hidden

explanation: Great job thinking about patient environments! In a home, closed doors and isolation make it much easier to hide abuse than in a busy, open hospital ward.

question: What is the fastest way to crash and bankrupt a working Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Conducting regular monthly stock counts of all tablets
options.B: Giving out large quantities of medicines on uncontrolled credit
options.C: Keeping the pharmacy store clean, dry, and well-ventilated
options.D: Buying drugs in large bulk quantities directly from manufacturers

explanation: You nailed it! If people take drugs on credit and never pay back, the cash never returns to buy new stock, and the fund collapses.

question: In community health nursing, who is considered your primary client?

options.A: Only the head of the household
options.B: Private paying clients in clinics
options.C: Patients admitted to the surgical ward
options.D: The entire community or population

explanation: Exactly! The heart of public health nursing is treating the whole community—not just one person—as your main patient.

question: Why can it be tricky for nurses to spot clinical depression in physically disabled patients?

options.A: Physical therapists handle all mental health evaluations
options.B: Depression always presents with loud, aggressive outbursts
options.C: Patients with disabilities are legally barred from taking antidepressants
options.D: Symptoms like fatigue and sleep changes can overlap with physical illness

explanation: It's tricky because chronic physical issues already cause tiredness and trouble sleeping. It takes extra care to notice when those signs point to worsening mental health.

question: As a nurse, why should you carefully review published research before using it?

options.A: To decide if findings are safe and appropriate to apply to patients
options.B: To find grammatical errors in academic writing
options.C: To publish their own papers in foreign journals
options.D: To prove that researchers always make mistakes

explanation: You've got this! Checking research helps you figure out what is actually safe and helpful to bring into your daily ward routine.

question: Why is family planning counseling a key part of post-abortion care?

options.A: To ensure the client conceives again within the next month
options.B: To fulfill a hospital administrative requirement unrelated to health
options.C: To help the client prevent future unintended pregnancies and repeat procedures
options.D: To punish the client for experiencing a pregnancy loss

explanation: Offering contraception right away helps clients protect their health and avoid another unplanned pregnancy down the line. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h7)

question: Why do we focus more on prevention than cure in MCH programs?

options.A: Preventive care stops complications before they become life-threatening
options.B: Curative care requires expensive machinery that is always unavailable
options.C: Curative care is prohibited in primary health care clinics
options.D: Preventive care completely eliminates the need for any medications

explanation: Spot-on! Stopping an illness before it takes root saves lives and energy compared to fighting an advanced disease later on. Prevention is your best tool as a nurse.

question: A nursing school wants to help students dealing with the digital divide. What should they do first?

options.A: Lengthen the required clinical hours at the base hospital ward
options.B: Provide accessible computer labs and reliable internet access on campus
options.C: Remove all digital assignments from the nursing curriculum
options.D: Increase the difficulty of the weekly online quizzes

explanation: Setting up on-site computer labs and internet directly bridges the resource gap for students who don't have personal tech at home. Excellent problem-solving!

question: A patient after abdominal surgery tries to avoid taking deep breaths because it hurts. What complication are they most likely heading toward?

options.A: Atelectasis
options.B: Muscle contractures
options.C: Pressure ulcers
options.D: Renal failure

explanation: Well done! Shallow breathing stops the tiny air sacs (alveoli) from opening up fully, which can cause them to collapse and lead to atelectasis or pneumonia. Encouraging deep breaths is key!

question: An 8-month-old baby comes to the clinic having missed their 14-week doses. What should you do?

options.A: Restart the entire immunization series from the very beginning
options.B: Continue the schedule from where they stopped using catch-up principles
options.C: Give only adult-strength boosters to make up for lost time
options.D: Wait until the child turns one year old before administering any new vaccines

explanation: No need to restart! Immunization schedules are cumulative. Just use catch-up principles to pick up right where they left off.

question: Which of the following is NOT a permissible reason for a nurse to breach patient confidentiality in routine clinical settings?

options.A: Specific legal mandates or court orders requiring disclosure for public safety
options.B: Assisted partner notification conducted with the client's explicit consent and safety clearance
options.C: Immediate threat of severe harm where professional intervention is legally required
options.D: Curiosity from extended family members who want to know why the patient is visiting the clinic

explanation: Family curiosity is never a valid reason to breach confidentiality; privacy rights protect patients from unauthorized snooping. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h8)

question: Why is it smart to check back on a patient shortly after giving them a new intravenous drug?

options.A: To ask if they want extra hospital bed sheets
options.B: To remind the patient to pay their hospital treatment bills
options.C: To collect the empty plastic tray and disposable syringe
options.D: To check for immediate adverse reactions or allergic responses

explanation: IV drugs act fast! Popping back in lets you catch sudden allergic reactions or low blood pressure early when you can easily help.

question: Why are Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs) sometimes prescribed for severe hypochondriasis?

options.A: To lower the overall intensity of obsessive health worries and treat depression
options.B: To cure any undiagnosed viral infections hiding in the bloodstream
options.C: To cause mild sedation so the patient sleeps through doctor appointments
options.D: To physically block pain receptors in the muscles and internal organs

explanation: SSRIs help balance the brain chemicals tied to anxiety and obsession, making it much easier for the patient to participate in therapy.

question: How does benzonatate work to stop a patient's cough?

options.A: Anesthetizing stretch receptors in the respiratory tract
options.B: Depressing the heart rate to lower blood pressure
options.C: Paralyzing the muscles of the abdominal wall
options.D: Blocking histamine receptors in the nasal passages

explanation: Benzonatate acts locally by gently numbing the stretch receptors in the airways, stopping the urge to cough right at the source.

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant women about cramps during antenatal visits?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any further doctor checkups
options.B: Instructing the mother to avoid all physical movement
options.C: Helping the patient tell normal discomforts from warning signs
options.D: Teaching the patient how to perform an ultrasound scan

explanation: Good health education helps mothers feel confident, knowing what is normal while staying alert to red flags. You're thinking like a great community nurse!

question: Why do unit managers keep a close eye on daily supplies and medications?

options.A: To sell extra medications to patients for extra cash
options.B: To keep the storage room locked permanently
options.C: To prevent shortages and reduce unnecessary waste
options.D: To ensure the ward has zero items stored at any time

explanation: Spot on! Keeping track of inventory makes sure the ward always has what it needs without wasting valuable hospital supplies.

question: How can transparent financial reporting improve PTA participation?

options.A: It ensures that teachers no longer pay any school dues
options.B: It stops the government from inspecting school accounts
options.C: It reduces the total number of students in the classroom
options.D: It builds trust and encourages more parents to support projects

explanation: When parents see that their contributions are used honestly for projects like school clinics, their willingness to support grows. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why do people often compare a research design to an architect's drawing?

options.A: It dictates the physical height and color of the hospital
options.B: It gives direction and structural stability to the investigation
options.C: It is only created by engineers rather than healthcare workers
options.D: It is drawn on large blueprint paper using physical ink

explanation: Just like a builder needs a solid blueprint to put up a safe house, a researcher needs a design to keep the study structured and valid.

question: What is the primary tool nurses use to map out a family health history across generations?

options.A: A Punnett square
options.B: A blood glucose log
options.C: A genogram
options.D: A karyotype chart

explanation: A genogram is a visual family tree that helps nurses map inherited diseases and health patterns across generations. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why are bedside nurses so great at leading quality improvement?

options.A: They are the only ones who understand data statistics
options.B: They handle the hospital's financial budgets
options.C: They spend their time sitting in administrative offices
options.D: They see daily workflow issues and safety risks firsthand

explanation: Spot on! Because you're right there at the bedside delivering care every day, you know better than anyone where things slow down or break. Your daily experience is a superpower!

question: Which blood vessels act as control valves to regulate blood flow into local tissues?

options.A: Lymphatic ducts
options.B: Arterioles
options.C: Large arteries
options.D: Vena cavae

explanation: Arterioles have muscular walls that contract or relax to control the volume of blood entering capillary beds. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h3)

question: A patient with thick, sticky mucus blocking their airways is most likely to be prescribed which type of inhalable medication?

options.A: Beta-blockers
options.B: Anticoagulants
options.C: Vasopressors
options.D: Mucolytics

explanation: Mucolytics are specifically designed to break down and thin thick respiratory secretions so they can be cleared more easily. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h4)

question: Expired medications and leftover vaccines belong to which waste category?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General domestic waste

explanation: You got it! Drugs and medicines always fall under pharmaceutical waste guidelines. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is a very common physical injury that happens even during proper, high-quality chest compressions?

options.A: Skull fracture
options.B: Spinal dislocation
options.C: Rib fractures
options.D: Lung collapse

explanation: Don't be alarmed if you feel a crack! Pushing hard enough to save a life often causes minor rib or sternum fractures—saving the life comes first.

question: What is the internationally recognized age below which a union is considered child marriage?

options.A: Below 16 years
options.B: Below 21 years
options.C: Below 15 years
options.D: Below 18 years

explanation: Any marriage involving a person under the age of 18 is classified as child or early marriage according to global standards. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T9#GNS312_U1_T9_h1)

question: When is it safe to have unprotected sex using the basal body temperature method without risking pregnancy?

options.A: Throughout the entire first week of the menstrual cycle
options.B: During the morning when the temperature spike is first noticed
options.C: On the exact day the temperature drops to its lowest point
options.D: After the temperature has remained elevated for three consecutive mornings

explanation: Three days of higher temperatures confirm that ovulation has already happened and the egg is gone. Safe zone unlocked!

question: What percentage of nephrons in the human kidney are classified as cortical nephrons?

options.A: About 50 percent
options.B: About 99 percent
options.C: About 85 percent
options.D: About 15 percent

explanation: The vast majority of nephrons in a healthy human kidney are cortical nephrons located mostly in the outer cortex. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h4)

question: What common operational problem often strains the relationship between Nigerian hospitals and HMOs?

options.A: Delayed payments and capitation disbursements by the HMOs
options.B: Enrollees demanding to work as administrative staff in insurance offices
options.C: Hospitals refusing to admit any patients who have insurance
options.D: The government banning all private health insurance schemes

explanation: When HMOs delay remitting capitation or settling service claims, hospitals struggle financially to provide quality medications and care. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of industrial pasteurization?

options.A: To destroy disease-causing microbes in liquids like milk
options.B: To remove all water from canned vegetables
options.C: To freeze liquids solid for long-term storage
options.D: To add artificial colors and flavors to beverages

explanation: Pasteurization uses gentle heat to knock out dangerous germs in everyday drinks like milk without ruining the taste or quality.

question: Why is hand hygiene even more crucial for home nurses than hospital nurses?

options.A: Home health nurses do not wear gloves during procedures
options.B: Homes lack centralized sterile utility rooms and controlled hospital sanitation
options.C: Patients at home are completely immune to hospital germs
options.D: Soap and water are strictly forbidden in residential houses

explanation: Spot on! Because houses don't have hospital-grade sterilisation units, good old-fashioned hand hygiene is our best defense against germs.

question: What is cervicitis?

options.A: Infection of the uterine lining
options.B: Inflammation of the cervix
options.C: Overgrowth of normal vaginal flora
options.D: Scarring of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Cervicitis refers specifically to the inflammation of the mucosal and epithelial tissues of the cervix. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T14#GNS216_U5_T14_h1)

question: What is orthostatic hypotension?

options.A: A gradual increase in resting heart rate over time
options.B: A sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up
options.C: A sudden spike in blood sugar after eating meals
options.D: A permanent loss of feeling in the lower legs

explanation: Orthostatic hypotension occurs when blood pools in the lower body upon rising, causing a drop in blood pressure and subsequent dizziness. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h4)

question: Why do patients with advanced occupational lung diseases have an increased risk of heart failure?

options.A: Respiratory failure lowers the body temperature until the heart stops beating
options.B: The inhaled mineral dust travels directly into the heart muscle and clogs valves
options.C: Scarred lung tissue restricts blood flow, forcing the right heart to pump much harder
options.D: Lung damage causes the patient to drink excessive amounts of salty water

explanation: Destruction of the pulmonary capillary bed increases vascular resistance, putting immense strain on the right side of the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why do patients sometimes resist following a nursing care plan?

options.A: Fear, misunderstanding, or a perceived loss of personal control
options.B: An excessive desire to follow medical instructions perfectly
options.C: Complete agreement with the community nurse
options.D: Too much free time available during the day

explanation: Resistance is usually just fear or a worry that they are losing their independence. Once you understand that, it's easier to help them!

question: How does the ICD stand apart from the DSM?

options.A: The ICD ignores symptom duration when diagnosing mental health
options.B: The ICD covers all general medical conditions, not just mental disorders
options.C: The ICD is published by a local psychiatric association
options.D: The ICD is only used for nursing documentation in emergency rooms

explanation: While the DSM focuses purely on mental health, the ICD is a massive catalog covering every known human illness and injury.

question: Why is electrical muscle stimulation sometimes used during physical rehabilitation?

options.A: To permanently replace voluntary muscle contraction
options.B: To help re-educate and stimulate muscles that have lost nerve signaling
options.C: To provide general systemic pain relief like a warm bath
options.D: To rapidly increase red blood cell production

explanation: Spot on! Gentle electrical pulses can help wake up and contract muscles that aren't receiving normal signals from the brain yet.

question: Which of these is NOT a major long-term complication of uncontrolled high blood pressure?

options.A: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Chronic kidney disease
options.C: Stroke
options.D: Myocardial infarction

explanation: Correct! Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition involving the pancreas, not something directly caused by high blood pressure.

question: Which of these is a very common hazard you might spot in a patient's home?

options.A: Loose floor rugs and cluttered walkways
options.B: Wall-mounted oxygen supply pipelines
options.C: Permanently locked emergency exit doors
options.D: Standardized hospital call bells in every room

explanation: Houses aren't built like hospitals! Everyday obstacles like loose rugs or poor lighting easily cause patient falls. Always scan the floor during home visits.

question: Why is the infant mortality rate considered a sensitive indicator of a community's general health status?

options.A: It shows the exact number of elderly people suffering from chronic heart conditions
options.B: It measures the total financial wealth of households in the region
options.C: It reflects the quality of maternal and child health services and living conditions
options.D: It is the easiest statistic for local government officials to calculate manually

explanation: Infant survival depends heavily on clean water, nutrition, and good healthcare, making it a reliable mirror of overall community well-being. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the main focus of 'validity' when creating a research tool?

options.A: Whether the tool gives the exact same score every single time
options.B: How many patients can complete the form in ten minutes
options.C: How cheap the research instrument is to buy in bulk
options.D: Whether the tool measures what it is supposed to measure

explanation: Validity is about hitting the bullseye! If you want to measure patient anxiety, a valid tool actually captures anxiety, not physical pain or hunger.

question: What is the main goal of the discussion section in a research paper?

options.A: To detail the exact steps of the data collection process
options.B: To present raw statistical data without any interpretation
options.C: To list the demographic characteristics of the participants
options.D: To explain the meaning of the results and their implications

explanation: You've got this! The discussion section takes those dry numbers and explains what they actually mean for everyday nursing practice.

question: What does the term 'crossed signs' mean when talking about brain stem injuries?

options.A: Loss of vision in both eyes combined with hearing loss
options.B: Complete paralysis of both arms and both legs equally
options.C: Facial deficits on one side with body deficits on the other
options.D: Inability to breathe while maintaining normal heart rate

explanation: Crossed signs happen when cranial nerve damage affects the face on one side, while other pathway damages affect the body on the opposite side. It creates a crossed pattern of symptoms!

question: Which symptom suggests a patient's pain is from retained tissue rather than normal recovery?

options.A: Temporary loss of appetite for a few hours
options.B: Mild lower back ache that goes away with rest
options.C: Itchy skin rash on the arms and chest
options.D: Severe cramping accompanied by heavy bleeding or large clots

explanation: If tissue is left behind, the uterus squeezes extra hard to push it out, causing intense cramps and heavy bleeding. Always watch out for this red flag!

question: How can a nurse researcher best cut down on sampling bias?

options.A: Keep the sample size as small as possible to save time
options.B: Use random selection methods and clear inclusion criteria
options.C: Select only friends and family members who agree to participate
options.D: Ignore patients who do not fit the desired research outcome

explanation: You got it! Randomization and clear rules about who can join keep things fair and help your sample truly represent the wider population.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to maintain high data quality?

options.A: Relying entirely on memory without writing down field notes
options.B: Training field staff properly before surveys begin
options.C: Conducting routine spot-checks and data audits
options.D: Using clear and pre-tested data collection forms

explanation: Human memory is fallible; failing to record data immediately in the field leads to severe omissions and errors. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T1#GNS313_U4_T1_h4)

question: What is the best dietary advice for a patient recovering from a bout of diarrhoea?

options.A: Gradually introduce bland foods and avoid fatty or spicy items
options.B: Immediately return to eating high-fiber raw vegetables and nuts
options.C: Avoid eating all foods completely for at least one full week
options.D: Consume large amounts of whole milk and dairy products daily

explanation: When the gut is healing, it needs an easy time. Bland foods are gentle, whereas fats, spices, and heavy dairy can stir things right back up again.

question: Why does damaged joint cartilage take such a long time to heal?

options.A: It lacks a direct blood supply
options.B: It is constantly dissolved by joint fluid
options.C: It has too many active breakdown cells
options.D: It contains no cells at all

explanation: Because cartilage doesn't have its own blood vessels, healing nutrients have to slowly ooze in from nearby tissues, making repair a very slow process.

question: How do anticoagulant medications help treat a deep vein thrombosis?

options.A: By lowering the patient's cholesterol and blood sugar
options.B: By instantly widening the blocked vein
options.C: By melting existing clots away within minutes
options.D: By stopping the clot from getting bigger while the body heals

explanation: A common myth is that anticoagulants 'dissolve' clots like magic. Actually, they act as blood thinners that stop the clot from growing bigger, giving your body time to break it down naturally and safely.

question: Before you start collecting data for a community diagnosis, what is usually the very first step?

options.A: Securing administrative clearance and mobilizing stakeholders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Writing the final evaluation report for the ministry
options.D: Treating all sick children with antibiotics

explanation: You always want to respect local authority! Getting permission and greeting community leaders comes first before marching in with clipboards.

question: How do people usually catch an Ascaris infection?

options.A: Swallowing infective eggs from contaminated soil or food
options.B: Wading in slow-moving freshwater streams
options.C: Eating poorly cooked freshwater fish
options.D: Being bitten by infected mosquitoes

explanation: It spreads through the fecal-oral route—usually when microscopic eggs from contaminated soil or unwashed food get swallowed.

question: A mother asks how to check if a small toy is safe from being a choking hazard for her baby. What is a quick rule of thumb?

options.A: If the toy is made of painted wood, it is automatically safe for teething.
options.B: If the infant can lift the toy with one hand, it poses a choking hazard.
options.C: If the toy has no removable batteries, it cannot cause choking.
options.D: If the toy fits entirely inside a toilet paper roll, it is too small and unsafe.

explanation: You nailed it! The cardboard toilet paper roll trick is a classic, easy way to test if an object is small enough to block a baby's airway.

question: Why does calling FGM a human rights violation make such a big difference in healthcare and law?

options.A: It makes prosecution of offenders completely unnecessary in local courts
options.B: It grants healthcare workers the right to perform the procedure safely
options.C: It redefines the practice from a tradition to a punishable act of violence
options.D: It removes the need for community education and legal penalties

explanation: You got it! Labeling FGM as a human rights abuse takes it out of the 'harmless culture' box, making it clear to everyone that it is harmful and unlawful.

question: What is the primary purpose of indirect nursing care technologies?

options.A: To support behind-the-scenes hospital operations and administrative tasks
options.B: To monitor patient vital signs directly at the skin surface
options.C: To replace bedside nurses during surgical procedures
options.D: To diagnose complex diseases without laboratory tests

explanation: Indirect care technologies handle logistics, scheduling, and inventory so that nurses spend less time on paperwork. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h1)

question: What shape is the anterior fontanelle (the front soft spot)?

options.A: Square-shaped
options.B: Oval-shaped
options.C: Diamond-shaped
options.D: Triangle-shaped

explanation: You nailed it! The front fontanelle is larger and diamond-shaped, which makes it a great landmark to spot during an exam.

question: What should you do if a patient's room is too dark when you are trying to check their skin?

options.A: Ask the patient to turn on all the household television sets.
options.B: Use a portable examination light to properly view the skin.
options.C: Skip the skin inspection until the patient visits the clinic.
options.D: Rely entirely on touch and palpation to detect any skin rashes.

explanation: Correct! Good lighting is a must for spotting subtle rashes, bruises, or color changes that you'd miss in a dark room.

question: What should you check first if a patient with a catheter suddenly stops passing urine?

options.A: Pull the catheter out right away and put in a new one
options.B: Give a fast dose of an intravenous water pill
options.C: Check the tubing for kinks, twists, or someone lying on it
options.D: Call the doctor to report total kidney failure

explanation: Great nursing instinct! Most of the time, urine stops flowing simply because the tube is bent or pinched. Always check the lines first!

question: A community nurse organizes a routine immunization outreach program for infants in a remote village. Which category of care does this activity fall under?

options.A: Preventive care
options.B: Curative care
options.C: Palliative care
options.D: Rehabilitative care

explanation: Immunizing infants protects them from contracting infectious diseases, which makes it a core preventive healthcare activity. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h3)

question: What is the main job of the urethra in both men and women?

options.A: Producing fluids that make up the liquid portion of semen
options.B: Transporting urine from the bladder to the outside of the body
options.C: Filtering waste products out of the bloodstream to form urine
options.D: Storing urine until the bladder is ready to release it

explanation: You've got this! Think of the urethra simply as a drainage pipe that carries urine from the base of the bladder out of the body.

question: What does the lab usually do if the name on a specimen tube doesn't match the request form?

options.A: Fix the typo themselves without informing the ward
options.B: Reject the specimen and request a new collection
options.C: Call the doctor to guess which patient it belongs to
options.D: Process the sample anyway using the bed number

explanation: Labs have zero tolerance for mismatched names because it's a huge safety hazard. They will throw it out and ask for a fresh sample.

question: For how many months should a baby be exclusively breastfed?

options.A: The first 9 months of life
options.B: The entire first year of life
options.C: The first 6 months of life
options.D: The first 3 months of life

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, food, and protection a baby needs for their first 6 solid months.

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful way for families to show love when a patient stops eating?

options.A: Forcing the patient to swallow liquid supplements
options.B: Moistening dry lips with a swab
options.C: Sitting quietly and holding hands
options.D: Giving gentle hand massages

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Forcing supplements causes distress. Love is best shown through touch, wet swabs for dry lips, and quiet presence.

question: How do Chi-Square hypotheses usually handle direction?

options.A: They are typically non-directional and test for any association
options.B: They must always predict a positive linear direction
options.C: They only evaluate single continuous variables
options.D: They measure the exact numerical difference between means

explanation: Keep it up! Standard Chi-Square tests simply ask if a connection exists overall, without needing to guess whether it goes up or down.

question: When should you refer a reproductive health patient to a specialist counselor?

options.A: When emotional distress exceeds basic supportive nursing care
options.B: Whenever the patient asks what medication they are taking
options.C: Only after the patient has completed all surgical treatments
options.D: Before the nurse performs any physical assessment

explanation: Spot on! While you provide great initial comfort, deep or complex emotional distress is best handled by mental health specialists.

question: Why is a home care nurse in a great position to notice a client's emotional and mental state?

options.A: They enter private spaces where clients feel comfortable letting their guard down
options.B: They focus exclusively on mental health rather than physical care
options.C: They have advanced psychiatric training required by law
options.D: They spend less time with clients than hospital nurses do

explanation: Visiting someone in their own home lets you see the real picture. Clients are often more relaxed and open in their personal space than they'd ever be in a busy clinic ward.

question: Why do many patients like to use complementary therapies along with their regular care?

options.A: Because they are always cheaper than conventional drugs
options.B: To replace all standard prescription medications permanently
options.C: To align with personal wellness values and address chronic issues
options.D: Because orthodox doctors mandate them in all hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Patients often look for a whole-person approach that fits their personal beliefs, especially when dealing with long-term health challenges.

question: Which hormone relaxes the muscles of the urinary tract during pregnancy, causing the ureters to widen?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles all over the body. During pregnancy, this causes the tubes carrying urine from the kidneys to widen. You've got this!

question: How does a shortened fallopian tube typically affect how a fertilized egg travels to the uterus?

options.A: It causes rapid transit, leading to early entry into the uterus
options.B: It traps the embryo permanently in the isthmus
options.C: It reverses the muscular waves pushing it backward
options.D: It completely stops all ciliary movement in the tubal lining

explanation: Because there is less distance to travel, the fertilized egg rushes through too quickly and reaches the uterus before it is fully ready to implant.

question: Why should a nurse avoid abruptly stopping a patient's compulsive ritual?

options.A: It immediately destroys the therapeutic trust built with the doctor
options.B: It breaks hospital legal regulations regarding patient property rights
options.C: It causes permanent physical paralysis in the patient's limbs
options.D: It triggers severe panic and dangerous anxiety spikes in the patient

explanation: Correct! Compulsions are their current shield against panic; snatching that away suddenly throws them into massive distress.

question: Who is the main officer at the Local Government level in charge of gathering disease reports?

options.A: Chief Pharmacist of the Federal Teaching Hospital
options.B: Local Government Area Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer
options.C: National Minister of Finance and Budget Planning
options.D: Director of Immigration and Border Control

explanation: Spot on! The LGA DSNO is the key person coordinating surveillance and collecting initial reports from health facilities in the area.

question: How do occupational health programs differ from regular hospital care?

options.A: They only handle severe physical trauma and surgeries
options.B: They focus heavily on prevention and work environments
options.C: They ignore mental health and focus strictly on machinery
options.D: They are managed exclusively by financial auditors

explanation: While hospitals treat people after they fall sick, occupational health steps in early to make the workplace itself safe so illnesses never happen in the first place. Makes total sense, right?

question: Which blood vessel brings blood directly into the glomerulus for filtering?

options.A: Peritubular capillary
options.B: Efferent arteriole
options.C: Renal vein
options.D: Afferent arteriole

explanation: Spot on! Think of the 'A' in Afferent as 'Arriving'—it brings blood into the glomerulus, while the efferent arteriole carries it away.

question: Which everyday habit causes a person to swallow extra air?

options.A: Sleeping on the left side
options.B: Chewing gum
options.C: Eating green leafy vegetables
options.D: Drinking plain water slowly

explanation: Chewing gum makes you swallow air without realizing it, which adds to the gas buildup in your tummy. Good to know for patient teaching!

question: Which type of family planning method is generally considered safest for a breastfeeding mother in the early weeks?

options.A: Progestin-only methods
options.B: Emergency morning-after pills
options.C: High-dose estrogen patches
options.D: Combined oral contraceptives

explanation: Progestin-only options (like mini-pills or certain injectables) won't mess with her breastmilk supply, making them a great choice for nursing mums. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h8)

question: What is the main goal of doing an endocrine stimulation test?

options.A: To cure the patient of chronic hormone overproduction
options.B: To check if a target gland can respond to a hormone
options.C: To remove antibodies attacking the endocrine tissues
options.D: To force the pituitary gland to shrink in size

explanation: We give a little push (a synthetic hormone) to see if a sleepy or struggling gland can wake up and respond like it's supposed to.

question: Which handy tool do nurses use to track changes in a patient's level of consciousness?

options.A: Pain numeric rating scale
options.B: Body mass index chart
options.C: Apgar scoring system
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: Great clinical instinct! The Glasgow Coma Scale gives us a quick, standard way to check eye, verbal, and motor responses.

question: Why is community ownership so important for the long-term success of health projects?

options.A: It guarantees that the clinic will make a profit from drug sales.
options.B: It removes all responsibilities from the shoulders of community nurses.
options.C: Locals will sustain and protect the program after external support ends.
options.D: Government health budgets will no longer be needed at all.

explanation: Exactly! When the community feels the project is theirs, they will keep it running strong long after outsiders pack up and leave.

question: Which of the following is a major drawback or limitation of using research checklists?

options.A: They cost more money than any other research tool
options.B: They are completely impossible to analyze statistically
options.C: They take months of training to read and write
options.D: They can oversimplify complex clinical situations

explanation: Checklists are great, but ticking boxes can sometimes strip away the rich details of a complex clinical scenario.

question: How does a psychiatric nurse help reduce community stigma regarding mental illness?

options.A: By keeping all psychiatric diagnoses strictly hidden from the public
options.B: By admitting every stressed individual into a secure hospital ward
options.C: By telling patients to ignore their symptoms and stay busy
options.D: By educating families that mental conditions are treatable medical illnesses

explanation: Education helps remove shame by teaching the community that mental health challenges are medical issues, just like physical conditions. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical limitation of questionnaire-based studies?

options.A: The potential for respondents to misunderstand written items
options.B: The lack of opportunity to ask follow-up probing questions
options.C: The ability to immediately observe complex clinical healing processes
options.D: The risk of receiving very low response rates from participants

explanation: Questionnaires collect self-reported written data; they do not allow a nurse to physically observe clinical healing processes firsthand. You are crushing these questions!

question: When might a doctor choose a barium enema instead of a standard colonoscopy?

options.A: When the patient needs an immediate tissue biopsy of a mass
options.B: When a tight narrowing (stricture) stops the colonoscope from passing through
options.C: When looking at blood vessels is the only goal
options.D: When the patient has an active bowel tear needing emergency surgery

explanation: Liquid barium can flow past narrow spots that a camera scope cannot safely squeeze through, helping doctors see what is happening further up the bowel.

question: Why must a nurse stay right at the bedside until the patient swallows their pills?

options.A: To clean up any empty water cups left on the bedside table
options.B: To measure the exact time it takes for the liver to metabolize the pill
options.C: To ensure the patient actually takes the drug and does not hoard it
options.D: To chat with the patient about their daily recovery progress

explanation: Staying present keeps your patient safe. It guarantees they actually swallowed the medication instead of hiding it under their tongue or saving it for later.

question: Why is taking folic acid supplements so important in the early stages of pregnancy?

options.A: To increase the mother's blood volume
options.B: To stop maternal morning sickness
options.C: To strengthen the baby's tooth enamel
options.D: To prevent neural tube defects

explanation: Spot on! Folic acid helps form the baby's neural tube early on, protecting the brain and spinal cord from serious issues.

question: Why is a pulse oximeter such a helpful tool when assessing a breathless patient?

options.A: It measures the exact pressure of carbon dioxide in the blood.
options.B: It replaces the need to count the patient's respiratory rate.
options.C: It gives a quick, painless way to check oxygen levels in the blood.
options.D: It determines the primary infectious organism in the lungs.

explanation: The little finger probe lets you check oxygen levels instantly without poking the patient with a needle. Very handy in busy wards!

question: How is an idiosyncratic drug reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.A: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose of medicine.
options.B: It can be easily predicted by checking standard blood test results.
options.C: It is a mild response that always goes away without any treatment.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and does not depend on the drug dose.

explanation: Think of an idiosyncratic reaction as a surprise response! Unlike normal side effects that we expect, these happen out of nowhere due to a patient's unique body makeup, not because of a high dose. You've got this!

question: How long should children wash their hands with soap to properly get rid of germs?

options.A: Twenty seconds
options.B: Ten seconds
options.C: One hour
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Twenty seconds is the magic number! Singing a short song helps kids scrub long enough to break down the germs on their skin.

question: What is the primary goal of nursing management in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Working through staff and resources to meet patient care goals
options.B: Writing medical diagnoses for admitted patients
options.C: Handling hospital finance and billing exclusively
options.D: Conducting laboratory research on new medications

explanation: Nursing management focuses on organizing people and tools to deliver safe, effective patient care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T4#GST321_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is a key role of the community health nurse in home delivery selection?

options.A: Financing the building of new maternity wards
options.B: Prescribing major surgical operations at home
options.C: Acting as an educator and clinical gatekeeper
options.D: Making decisions without consulting the mother

explanation: The nurse educates the family and screens candidates to ensure safety standards are strictly maintained. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h8)

question: Which group of organs gets drugs distributed to them the fastest because of high blood supply?

options.A: Ligaments and tendons
options.B: Bones and resting muscle
options.C: Heart, brain, and liver
options.D: Skin and fatty tissue

explanation: Vial organs get a huge share of the blood pumped by the heart, meaning circulating drugs arrive there almost instantly!

question: Why must nurses watch a mother and newborn extra closely immediately after delivery?

options.A: A high proportion of maternal and newborn deaths happen within the first 48 hours
options.B: The mother is usually discharged home immediately without any risk
options.C: Hormonal changes stop completely after the placenta is delivered
options.D: Newborns do not require feeding assistance until day three of life

explanation: The first 48 hours are the riskiest time for sudden bleeding, infections, or newborn collapse. Close monitoring keeps both mum and baby safe!

question: Which heart chamber pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary trunk?

options.A: Right atrium
options.B: Right ventricle
options.C: Left atrium
options.D: Left ventricle

explanation: The right ventricle is responsible for forcing deoxygenated blood out of the heart and into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h2)

question: A postpartum patient is bleeding heavily and showing signs of shock. What is the most urgent vascular access step?

options.A: Insert two large-bore intravenous cannulas for rapid fluid replacement
options.B: Administer oral rehydration salts slowly through a nasogastric tube
options.C: Set up a single fine-needle peripheral line for routine daily hydration
options.D: Collect a midstream urine sample to check for urinary tract infection

explanation: In an emergency, large-bore IV lines let you pump in fluids and blood fast enough to rescue her blood pressure and beat shock.

question: What do we study in microbiology?

options.A: The structural anatomy of multicellular forest plants
options.B: The breeding and management of large domesticated livestock
options.C: Organisms too small to see without a microscope
options.D: The chemical composition of rocks and mineral deposits

explanation: Microbiology is simply the study of tiny life forms like bacteria and viruses that need lenses to be seen clearly. You've got this!

question: What is the primary setting for home health care services?

options.A: A long-term nursing facility
options.B: A specialized tertiary hospital
options.C: An outpatient community clinic
options.D: The patient's private residence

explanation: Home health care specifically delivers medical and nursing services directly to where the patient lives. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is supervised exercise an important part of cardiac rehabilitation after a heart attack?

options.A: It guarantees that plaque will instantly dissolve out of every blocked artery
options.B: It safely strengthens the heart muscle and improves overall cardiovascular endurance
options.C: It stops the nervous system from ever experiencing emotional stress
options.D: it completely eliminates the need to ever take heart medications again

explanation: Gradual, monitored exercise helps the heart adapt and work more efficiently without putting the patient in danger. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h9)

question: What is the best first step for a nurse leader when staff are fighting or disagreeing?

options.A: Ignoring the disagreement until staff resolve it independently
options.B: Reassigning both staff members to opposite shifts immediately
options.C: Addressing the issue promptly through collaborative problem-solving
options.D: Issuing a formal disciplinary warning to all parties involved

explanation: Tackling conflicts early with open talk helps find the root cause before a small misunderstanding ruins teamwork on the ward.

question: What do the letters in the SMART goal-setting framework stand for?

options.A: Simple, Medical, Active, Realistic, Total
options.B: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, Time-bound
options.C: Safe, Meaningful, Accessible, Rapid, Tender
options.D: Systematic, Manual, Analytical, Routine, Tested

explanation: Spot on! SMART goals help nurses and patients set clear, realistic, and trackable targets for recovery.

question: What does 'feasibility' mean when you are checking if a research topic is practical?

options.A: Proving that the research will definitely win an international award
options.B: Ensuring the study topic sounds impressive to senior professors
options.C: Having enough time, money, and resources to complete the study
options.D: Getting permission to skip data collection if things get busy

explanation: Feasibility is just asking: 'Can we realistically pull this study off with the time and materials we have?'

question: Why do doctors treat active tuberculosis with several drugs at once instead of just one?

options.A: To counteract the severe sedative side effects of rifampin
options.B: To prevent the bacteria from developing drug resistance
options.C: To speed up the healing process so drugs are only taken for days
options.D: To completely eliminate normal flora in the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: Hitting TB bacteria with multiple drugs makes it super hard for them to mutate and survive. Multi-drug therapy is a lifesaver!

question: How does school-based health education impact the wider community?

options.A: Parents lose responsibility for teaching their children
options.B: Communities stop building local health clinics entirely
options.C: Local hospitals experience a permanent drop in staffing
options.D: Children take healthy habits home to their families

explanation: Students act as health messengers, sharing hygiene and nutrition practices learned at school with their families at home. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h6)

question: An older adult suddenly reports muffled hearing in one ear. What simple cause should you check for first?

options.A: A ruptured tympanic membrane from aging
options.B: Permanent damage to the auditory nerve
options.C: Impacted earwax blocking the canal
options.D: Degeneration of the cochlear hair cells

explanation: Always look for the simplest, most treatable cause first! A buildup of earwax (cerumen) is super common and easy to fix.

question: How does a nurse act as a true advocate for an adolescent patient?

options.A: By reporting every minor detail of counseling sessions to village elders
options.B: By charging extra fees for confidential consultations
options.C: By restricting access to health information to adults only
options.D: By protecting client confidentiality and defending their right to respectful care

explanation: You got it! As an advocate, you stand up for your young patients' rights to safe, private, and judgment-free care.

question: How does cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) help someone recovering from substance use?

options.A: By forcing them to forget all memories of their friends and family
options.B: By curing any physical infections caused by dirty needles
options.C: By helping them recognize personal triggers and build healthy coping mechanisms
options.D: By replacing their natural blood chemistry with artificial synthetic hormones

explanation: CBT is fantastic because it trains the mind to spot what triggers cravings and teaches healthier ways to handle life's stress.

question: What is the main goal of having a 'unified command' during a local emergency?

options.A: To ensure all responding agencies coordinate their tasks and know who is in charge
options.B: To centralize all funding in the hands of international donors
options.C: To prevent local volunteers from participating in search and rescue efforts
options.D: To allow the police force to take over all medical decisions in a hospital

explanation: Spot on! A unified command stops confusion by making sure every team knows their specific role and who is leading the response.

question: What does a Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment primarily look at?

options.A: Occupational history and retirement savings
options.B: Physical, functional, psychological, and social well-being
options.C: Surgical fitness for emergency organ transplants
options.D: Childhood developmental milestones

explanation: A Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment looks at the whole person—not just physical symptoms, but how they function, their mood, and their social life too.

question: What is the medical term for having an abnormally low platelet count, which increases a patient's risk of bleeding?

options.A: Anemia
options.B: Polycythemia
options.C: Thrombocytopenia
options.D: Leukemia

explanation: Well done! 'Thrombo' relates to clotting, 'cyto' to cells, and 'penia' means deficiency. Put it together, and thrombocytopenia means low platelets and bleeding risk.

question: What is the main job of the body's modulation phase in the pain pathway?

options.A: Deciding the emotional meaning of the injury in the brain
options.B: Converting tissue injury into a nerve impulse
options.C: Releasing natural body chemicals to turn down the pain signal
options.D: Carrying the electrical message up the spinal cord

explanation: Think of modulation as your body's built-in volume control! It releases substances like endorphins right in the spinal cord to quiet down the pain message.

question: What happens to the lower oesophageal sphincter in a patient with achalasia?

options.A: It fails to relax properly during swallowing
options.B: It moves upward into the chest cavity
options.C: It dissolves due to lack of local blood supply
options.D: It stays wide open all the time

explanation: In achalasia, the lower muscle valve stays stubbornly tight instead of opening up to let your food pass smoothly down into the stomach.

question: Why do we need intersectoral collaboration (working with other sectors) to achieve good public health?

options.A: Hospitals are solely responsible for fixing bad roads and cleaning rivers
options.B: The Ministry of Health cannot legally operate without approval from finance officers
options.C: Factors like education, agriculture, and housing directly influence overall health outcomes
options.D: Doctors must personally manage farming and school curriculum development

explanation: Health doesn't happen in a vacuum! Good housing, farming, and schools all play a huge role in keeping people healthy.

question: Why should a nurse gently rotate a PEG tube during routine stoma care?

options.A: To make sure the formula flows faster during meal times
options.B: To allow air to enter the stomach and reduce bloating
options.C: To prevent the internal bumper from sticking to the stomach wall
options.D: To help the external skin opening stretch wider for easier cleaning

explanation: Routine rotation stops tissue from growing over the internal retention bolster, preventing a serious complication called buried bumper syndrome. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which harmless temporary side effect do many clients experience during their first few months on the pill?

options.A: Permanent hair loss
options.B: Breakthrough spotting
options.C: Loss of vision
options.D: Sudden bone fractures

explanation: Spotting between periods can be scary for clients, but reassure them it's very normal as the body adjusts to the new hormones in the first few months.

question: A student nurse spots a missing decimal point on a drug order that looks way too high. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Contact the prescribing doctor to clarify the medication order before giving it
options.B: Ask another junior nurse to administer the drug since the order is official
options.C: Give the medication as written because doctors are never wrong
options.D: Administer half the dose to be safe and document the change in the chart

explanation: You are the patient's final safety net! Always pause and clarify any confusing or unsafe order with the prescriber before touching that medication cart.

question: What major mistake should you avoid when writing the results section?

options.A: Using tables and charts to summarize numerical findings
options.B: Including personal interpretations and opinions about the data
options.C: Reporting findings that go against the original hypothesis
options.D: Stating the exact statistical values found in the study

explanation: Keep the results section strictly factual! Save your opinions and deep meanings for the discussion chapter.

question: Which tiny structures form right next to the neural tube in an embryo to eventually build our skeletal muscles?

options.A: Somites
options.B: Neural crest cells
options.C: Lateral plate mesoderm
options.D: Pharyngeal arches

explanation: Somites are little blocks of tissue that line up next to the neural tube and develop into our skeletal muscles and bones. Great job learning the building blocks of the body!

question: What term describes the overlap between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Institutional friction
options.B: Operational burnout
options.C: Goal congruence
options.D: Budget deficit

explanation: 'Goal congruence' just means working in harmony—it's when your personal goals match up nicely with the hospital's goals.

question: What happens during 'data cleaning' after data collection?

options.A: Checking for entry mistakes, missing fields, and unusual outlier values
options.B: Translating all interview recordings into a different spoken language
options.C: Deleting any participant answers that do not support the hypothesis
options.D: Washing physical paper questionnaires with soap to remove hospital dust

explanation: Data cleaning means scanning your data for typos, blank spots, or weird errors before you start analyzing.

question: What HbA1c blood test result is generally used to diagnose diabetes?

options.A: 8.0% or higher
options.B: 10.5% or higher
options.D: 6.5% or higher

explanation: An HbA1c of 6.5% or higher shows that blood sugar has been running high over the past three months. It's a key lab value you'll use all the time in practice!

question: Why is time considered so critical when dealing with emergency medical conditions?

options.A: Hospital regulations require fast bed turnover
options.B: Insurance companies will not pay for slow care
options.C: Doctors refuse to see patients who wait too long
options.D: Delays can lead to rapid deterioration and death

explanation: In critical emergencies, minutes matter because a failing body system quickly causes permanent harm or death if not supported. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which nutrient intake value is set high enough to cover almost all healthy people?

options.A: Estimated Energy Requirement (EER)
options.B: Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)
options.C: Estimated Average Requirement (EAR)
options.D: Tolerable Upper Intake Level (UL)

explanation: You're doing great! The RDA is set high up to make sure it meets the nutritional needs of about 97 to 98 percent of healthy folks.

question: Why do we need a multi-sectoral approach (involving health, legal, and community groups) to eliminate FGM in Nigeria?

options.A: Foreign donors refuse to fund local healthcare workers
options.B: Federal laws ban NGOs from working in rural areas
options.C: Traditional rulers want total control over all medical and school policies
options.D: No single strategy alone can tackle such deep-rooted social and legal barriers

explanation: Brilliant! Because FGM touches on culture, law, health, and social norms, lasting change requires a teamwork approach across laws, healthcare, and local communities.

question: You wear sterile gloves and a mask while putting in a urinary catheter. Which link in the infection chain are you mainly trying to block?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Portal of entry
options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Infectious agent

explanation: Awesome! Using sterile barriers blocks germs from sneaking into vulnerable places like the urinary tract.

question: Why is it important to read the ingredient list on packaged foods?

options.A: To determine the precise market price of the item
options.B: To check for hidden sugars, sodium, and potential allergens
options.C: To calculate the exact weight of the empty container
options.D: To find out which factory manufactured the product

explanation: Ingredient lists reveal what is actually inside the food, helping patients avoid allergens and manage conditions like hypertension or diabetes. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h5)

question: A nurse is about to give a morning pill, but the patient's identification band is missing. What is the correct action?

options.A: Check the chart photo and give the medication to save time
options.B: Ask the patient to state their name and give the pill immediately
options.C: Ask another nurse to confirm the patient's face before giving the drug
options.D: Delay administration until a new identification band is placed on the patient

explanation: Two reliable identifiers like a properly fitted ID band are mandatory; guessing or relying solely on memory or roommates violates the right patient rule. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T2#GNS125_U4_T2_h2)

question: What is a key feature that makes a tertiary health facility unique?

options.A: It only handles uncomplicated outpatient malaria cases
options.B: It is the first point of contact in a rural village
options.C: It provides basic immunization only
options.D: It serves as a center for training and medical research

explanation: Tertiary hospitals (like our teaching hospitals) do double duty: they provide advanced patient care while training future healthcare heroes and conducting medical research.

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure 30 minutes after giving a blood pressure drug. Which nursing step is this?

options.A: Diagnosis
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Planning
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: Spot-checking to see if your nursing action actually worked is what evaluation is all about. Did the medicine do its job? Let's check!

question: Which lab value usually climbs when a patient has failing kidneys and can't clear protein waste?

options.A: Serum potassium levels
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Total body water weight

explanation: Since urea is the main waste product of protein, sluggish kidneys mean urea backs up, causing Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) levels to rise.

question: Why must nurses work alongside community leaders when trying to stop breast ironing?

options.A: Nurses lack the medical knowledge to identify physical scars
options.B: Local leaders hold influence and can help shift harmful cultural norms
options.C: Law enforcement officers refuse to speak directly with victims
options.D: Community leaders provide financial grants for hospital care

explanation: Engaging respected community figures helps communities accept change and abandon harmful practices from within. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h8)

question: Why does a toddler often need a higher weight-based drug dose than an infant?

options.A: Accelerated metabolic rates and faster clearance
options.B: Increased thickness of the skin layers
options.C: Complete maturation of the blood-brain barrier
options.D: Lower total body water percentage

explanation: Toddlers have super-active metabolic rates that process and clear certain drugs much faster than tiny infants do. Keep learning, you're doing great!

question: What is a common term for spinal nerve root compression caused by a herniated disc?

options.A: Encephalitis
options.B: Neuritis
options.C: Meningitis
options.D: Radiculopathy

explanation: Radiculopathy refers to pain, numbness, or weakness resulting from irritation or compression of a spinal nerve root. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T26#GNS211_U3_T26_h9)

question: Why do healthcare providers recommend breathable cotton underwear and loose clothing to prevent infections?

options.A: They increase local blood circulation to speed up tissue repair
options.B: They stop normal hormonal fluctuations from occurring
options.C: They prevent allergic reactions to harsh laundry detergents
options.D: They reduce moisture and heat buildup that encourages fungal growth

explanation: Yeast and bad bacteria love warm, dark, sweaty spaces. Breathable fabrics keep things cool, dry, and healthy! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h7)

question: What tool should the nurse use to check if a warm poultice is safe to apply?

options.A: A heavy weight pressed onto the mixture
options.B: A metal needle poked into the patient's arm
options.C: Their own inner wrist or a thermometer
options.D: A bright flashlight held close to the paste

explanation: Testing the temperature on the sensitive inner wrist helps verify the poultice is warm, not burning hot. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the main goal of doing a review of systems during an interview?

options.A: To perform a complete hands-on physical examination
options.B: To diagnose every chronic disease the patient has
options.C: To test the patient's knowledge of anatomy and physiology
options.D: To uncover symptoms the patient may have forgotten or omitted

explanation: You got it! The review of systems acts as a helpful safety net to catch any symptoms the patient forgot to mention.

question: What do we mean in healthcare when we say 'the physical environment creates the disability'?

options.A: Inaccessible buildings and transport disable people more than their actual medical impairment.
options.B: People with disabilities prefer staying indoors away from society.
options.C: Bad weather directly causes permanent physical paralysis.
options.D: Hospitals are solely responsible for causing new physical disabilities.

explanation: A person with a mobility challenge can thrive if buildings have ramps and elevators. Often, it's the lack of accessible infrastructure—not the body itself—that creates the barrier.

question: Why do nurses and healthcare workers face unique safety risks on the job?

options.A: They face constant exposure to infectious agents and physical strain
options.B: They are completely immune to common hospital-acquired infections
options.C: They rarely interact with patients who have contagious diseases
options.D: They spend most of their working hours sitting at a desk
